meta.scope: Records compatible with the Interpol DVI AM/PM forms (version 2023). Context of the record (disaster, or routine work on an individual case). Header of the forms: disaster (place, nature, date) or case (number, place, date of opening), and person (missing person of an AM record, sex of the remains of a PM record). Dental part: odontogram (field 630), arch-level removable dentures and the dental sections around it (fields 600 to 650: treating dentists, elements and images available, particulars, other observations, dentition, age estimate, quality control). Other non-dental sections to follow.
meta.author: Hadrien Diakonoff
meta.attribution: Perdrix, an open norm for filling in DVI records, by Hadrien Diakonoff, https://perdrix-dvi.org/ (CC BY 4.0). A modified version must say so and must not be called Perdrix: see NAME-POLICY.md in the repository.

changelog.changes: First public edition. The working history of the earlier versions is not published.

data_protection.definition: Metadata that make data-protection obligations applicable by the applications. The norm does not decide who may access what: that is the law of the issuing State.

identifiability_values.direct: identifies a natural person by itself (name, postal address, telephone, e-mail)
identifiability_values.indirect: can identify a natural person when combined with other data, or free text that may contain such data
identifiability_values.none: does not relate to an identifiable natural person by itself

dental_part.note: The odontogram and the dental findings are health data with a high identifying power: they are never freely shareable, whatever the identifiability of individual fields.

record_format.definition: Structure of an AM or PM record (header of the form and dental part). Teeth absent from 'teeth' are 'not yet filled'.

envelope.norm_version: version of the norm used to fill the record

record.context: record.context: disaster | routine (a record without context is a disaster record)
record.author: free text
record.document_date: AM: date of the most recent dental document; PM: date of examination
record.disaster: record.disaster: {name, place, nature, date} (place, nature and date: header of the Interpol forms); disaster records only
record.case: record.case: {number, disappearance_place (AM) | discovery_place (PM), opened}; routine records only
record.person: record.person: AM {family_name, forenames, birth_date, age (deduced from the date of birth and the date of the disaster), sex}; PM {sex}
record.generator: {name, version}: the application or tool that produced the record (traceability); set by the tool, never entered by the expert

envelope.signatures: list of signatures of this very content (see record_format.signature); absent from a record that has not been signed

dental.default_sources: list of dental.source, inherited by every tooth unless overridden; in an AM record it is deduced from the documents obtained when it is not entered

tooth.findings: list of {type: dental.finding, surfaces?, aspect?, subtype?, site?, provisional?, bridge_abutment?}

dental.comment: general comment of the dental part, free text; every comment is printed on the additional information page of the Interpol form (field 700), which is not specific to the dental part
dental.providers: AM, Interpol fields 600-605: list of dental.provider
dental.images: Interpol field 615: list of dental.image (one item per type)
dental.particulars: Interpol field 635: dental.particulars (deduced from the odontogram, can be corrected)
dental.dentition: Interpol field 645: dental.dentition (deduced from the teeth present, can be corrected)
dental.attachments: list of record_format.attachment: files annexed to the record (column b of the Interpol form)
dental.not_available: list of Interpol form field numbers (e.g. "615") for which data are not available (column a of the form): an absence of information, not to be confused with an empty section. Field 630 is the odontogram.

signature.definition: Electronic signature of a record: an expert attests, with a personal signing key, the content of the record at a given moment. Validation: the expert who completed the record declares it complete and checked. Countersignature: a second expert, other than the author of the validation, attests the same content (quality control, Interpol field 650). A signature proves that the content has not changed since it was signed by the holder of the key; it does not say who that person is (the key is known through the identity card handed to a manager).
signature.content: what is attested: the record without its 'signatures' member, written in the canonical form of RFC 8785 (JSON Canonicalization Scheme: keys sorted, no white space), hashed with SHA-256

fields.n: revision number: 1 at the first validation, one more at each new validation of a changed content; a countersignature carries the number of the revision it attests
fields.signed_at: ISO 8601 date and time, UTC, from the clock of the signing device
fields.norm_version: version of the norm of the signed content
fields.hash: SHA-256 of the content, hexadecimal, lower case
fields.author: {name, fingerprint, public_key}: public_key is the public signing key (JWK, curve P-256); fingerprint is the SHA-256, hexadecimal, of that key as an uncompressed point (65 bytes: 0x04, x, y)
fields.signature: signature of the statement, r then s (IEEE P1363, 64 bytes), in base64

signature.statement: what the key signs: the canonical form (RFC 8785) of {type, n, signed_at, norm_version, hash, author: {name, fingerprint}}, where type is 'perdrix.revision' for a validation and 'perdrix.countersignature' for a countersignature
signature.rules: a record carries at most one validation, and the countersignatures of that same content; every signature names the hash of the content it accompanies; a countersignature is not made with the key of the validation; earlier revisions are earlier records, each with its own signatures

attachment.definition: A file annexed to the record (photograph, radiograph, scanned document), kept by the application beside the record, encrypted like it. The record holds its description and the SHA-256 of its bytes: the signatures of the record therefore cover the file, and a file changed afterwards is detected. It is annexed to a section of the form that accepts attachments (section.attachments): on the Interpol form, the column b (annex) of that field is ticked.

fields.id: identifier of the file, unique in the record (letters, digits and '-')
fields.name: name of the file, as given by the device of the expert
fields.size: size of the file in bytes
fields.sha256: SHA-256 of the bytes of the file, hexadecimal, lower case
fields.at: where the file is annexed: the key of a section that accepts attachments; for a section with several rows on the form, the key, '.', then the row (images.panoramic, remains.fragments, providers.1, quality_control.2)
fields.caption: optional: free text describing the file
fields.added: optional: date the file was annexed (ISO 8601)

attachment.rows: section.attachments.rows: absent, the section has a single row (at = key); "entries", one row per entry of a list section, numbered from 1 up to form_slots; the name of an enumerated field, one row per value of that field (field 615: the type of image); a list of field names, one row per field (field 610)

record.context.definition: Context in which the record is made. It decides which sections of the envelope apply. A record that carries no context is a disaster record.

disaster.definition: Disaster: one event, several victims; the record carries the disaster it relates to.

routine.definition: Routine work: an individual case (one missing person, one unidentified body); the record carries the case it relates to.

record.disaster.definition: Disaster the record relates to. Its place, nature and date are written in the header of the Interpol forms; its name is not printed on the forms: it identifies the disaster, so that the records of one disaster can be grouped.

record.case.definition: Individual case the record relates to, in routine work: its number, the place where the person went missing (AM record) or where the body was found (PM record), and the date the case was opened. The header of the Interpol forms is written for disasters and has no room for these: an application that prints the form writes them on the additional information page.

record.person.definition: Person the record relates to, as written in the header of the Interpol forms. AM record: the missing person (family name, forenames, date of birth, age, sex). PM record: the sex of the unidentified remains; nothing else about the person is known at that stage.

dental.tooth.definition: Tooth identifier in FDI two-digit notation. The identity of the tooth is independent of the form box in which it is printed.
dental.tooth.form_box_rule: A primary tooth is printed in the box of the permanent tooth at the same position (5x->1x, 6x->2x, 7x->3x, 8x->4x), as instructed by the Interpol form.

dental.surface.definition: Tooth surface. Stored as a set, always serialised in canonical order.

O.definition: Occlusal surface (posterior teeth) or incisal edge (anterior teeth).

dental.status.definition: Status of the observation for one tooth position. Mandatory for every tooth in a validated record; an absent status means 'not yet filled'.

examined.definition: The position was examined; presence and findings are recorded.

examined_no_finding.definition: The tooth is present and nothing is to be recorded: no lesion, wear, restoration, treatment, appliance, jewellery or position anomaly.

no_information.definition: Nothing can be said about this position (e.g. missing jaw fragment, no ante-mortem record covering this tooth). This is not a negative finding.

dental.source.definition: Source on which the observation of a tooth is based. Several sources may be combined. Some combinations of findings are only valid when a given source is present (see rules of type requires_source).

photograph.definition: Photograph. Intra-oral mirror photographs are laterally inverted.

intraoral_scan.definition: Intra-oral optical scan (three-dimensional surface model of the teeth).

derivation.definition: In an AM record the sources are not entered: they are deduced from the treating dentists recorded (dental record) and from the documents and images obtained (radiographs, photographs). Sources entered in the record, if any, take precedence.

dental.presence.definition: Presence of the tooth at its position. Exactly one value when status = examined.

present.definition: Tooth (or its crown) present and visible in the oral cavity.

partially_erupted.definition: Tooth in the course of eruption, partially visible.

impacted_partially_visible.definition: Tooth emerging in the oral cavity but blocked in its eruption (mostly third molars).

unerupted.definition: Unerupted tooth whose presence is confirmed (typically radiographically).

not_visible.definition: Not visible clinically; presence cannot be confirmed without imaging (e.g. suspected unerupted tooth in a child).

root_remnant.definition: Only the root (or part of it) remains. Deliberately unspecific.

missing_am.definition: Tooth lost during life (healed or healing socket, or replaced by a prosthesis or implant). Covers extraction and agenesis: the cause is not recorded.

missing_pm.definition: Tooth lost after death (empty socket without healing).

dental.aspect.definition: Visible aspect of a restoration or prosthesis. Records what is observed (colour), not a material that cannot be verified. 'parent' gives the less specific value used by the comparator.

silver_metal.definition: Silver-coloured metal (amalgam for fillings; metal or preformed steel crown for crowns).

metal_ceramic.definition: Crown with a metal framework fully veneered with ceramic.

metal_with_facing.definition: Metal crown with a tooth-coloured facing or inlay on the visible surface only (older treatment).

dental.finding.definition: Finding on a tooth. A tooth carries a list of findings. allowed_presence lists the presence values compatible with the finding. observable_by lists the sources able to observe the finding directly; a dental record may report any finding.

substance_loss.definition: Loss of tooth substance whose origin is not specified (carious or not).

tooth_fracture.definition: Fracture of the tooth itself (not of the jaw, see group jaw_fracture).

filling.definition: Direct or indirect intracoronal restoration. Direct/indirect is not distinguished.

crown.definition: Prosthetic crown covering the whole clinical crown, on a natural tooth or on an implant.

pontic.definition: Bridge pontic replacing a missing tooth. A root remnant may remain underneath.

denture_tooth.definition: Tooth of a removable denture. A root remnant may remain underneath.

denture_attachment.definition: Retention device for a removable denture, on an implant or on a root.

root_post.definition: Post placed in a root canal to retain a restoration (screw post, cast post and core).

apicectomy.definition: Surgical resection of the root apex.

periodontal_pathology.definition: Periodontal disease affecting this tooth. Deliberately unspecific: mention only.

orthodontic_appliance.definition: Orthodontic appliance attached to or covering the tooth.

splint.definition: Bonded splint (retention wire) including this tooth. Segments are described by the group 'splint'.

rotation.definition: Rotation around the long axis, named after the direction in which the MESIAL surface has turned. Independent of the view and of the quadrant.

migration.definition: Displacement of the tooth along the arch.

dental.group.definition: Object linking several tooth positions. Teeth are listed in FDI notation.

bridge.definition: Fixed bridge. Members are the teeth carrying crown(bridge_abutment=true) or pontic; created automatically from contiguous members and splittable by the expert (17-14 vs 17-16 + 15-14).

splint.definition: Continuous segment of bonded splint. A broken splint gives several segments (e.g. 43-41 and 31-32).

crowding.definition: Crowding affecting a sector of the arch.

diastema.definition: Space between two adjacent present teeth.

jaw_fragment_missing.definition: Missing jaw fragment, containing 0 to n tooth positions. See also PM form, section 'Condition of the jaws' (fragments).

jaw_fracture.definition: Fracture line of the jaw, located between two adjacent tooth positions.

dental.arch.definition: Findings at the level of a whole arch. Other arch- or mouth-level remarks are recorded as free text.

removable_denture.definition: Removable denture on an arch. A complete denture is deduced when every tooth of the arch carries a denture tooth; third molars are optional, as they are often not set on a complete denture.

dental.provider.definition: Dentist or establishment that treated the missing person, with the period covered by the records and the documents obtained (AM records). A record may list any number of them; the Interpol form has room for two, the others are printed on the additional information page.

dental.remains.definition: Dental elements available for the post-mortem examination (PM records).

odontogram_prefill.definition: What the elements available say of the odontogram, entered for the expert by applications. A position is filled only when nothing is entered on it yet (neither on the permanent nor on the primary tooth of its box), never over an entry; when the elements available change, what was filled is withdrawn from the positions that hold it and nothing else. A jaw ticked edentulous: its positions are missing ante mortem. A jaw neither with teeth nor edentulous (not found, or found only in fragments), as soon as one of the fields of found or spared holds something: its positions other than the spared teeth (teeth of the fragments, isolated teeth) belong to a missing jaw fragment (status no information, R-D-005). Only the permanent positions of the jaws (quadrants) are filled.

dental.image.definition: Dental images available, by type, with the number of digital and non-digital images. As soon as one number is entered, the other types and numbers are 0.

dental.material.definition: Other materials obtained for the ante-mortem analysis (casts, appliances, written notes...), as free text.

dental.additional.definition: Additional information of the post-mortem dental examination: condition of the jaws and other information.

dental.particulars.definition: Summary of the prosthetic and endodontic particulars, as tick boxes. Each item is deduced from the odontogram and can be corrected by the expert; "other" has a detail entered when it is ticked. The detail is printed on the additional information page of the form (field 700).

dental.observation.definition: Other dental observations, as tick boxes, each with an optional detail entered when the box is ticked. Tooth wear and periodontal condition are deduced from the odontogram and can be corrected. The details are printed on the additional information page of the form (field 700).

dental.dentition.definition: Type of dentition, deduced from the teeth present in the mouth (primary only, permanent only, or both); a missing or unerupted tooth does not count. Can be corrected by the expert.

primary.definition: Only primary teeth are present in the mouth.

mixed.definition: Primary and permanent teeth are present in the mouth.

permanent.definition: Only permanent teeth are present in the mouth.

dental.age_estimate.definition: Dental age estimate of the post-mortem examination, as a range in years and/or months (PM records).

dental.quality_control.definition: Quality control of the dental part by one or two forensic odontologists, as printed on the form (names, dates). The electronic signatures of the record (validation by the author, countersignature by a second expert) are described by record_format.signature.

rules.rationale: "Sound" (no abnormality detected): nothing else may be entered (orthodontic appliance, splint and jewellery are incompatible).
A present sound tooth has no associated problem of any kind (no wear, substance loss, fracture, version, rotation...): extension to position anomalies, for consistency with the previous rule.
No information: no data about the position.
An examined position must have a presence.
Teeth in a missing jaw fragment default to status "no information" (can be changed).
Crown: the enamel defect is covered by the crown.
Crown: the occlusal surface is covered.
Crown: jewellery is bonded to the enamel.
Crown: attrition concerns a surface covered by the crown.
Crown: a coronal fracture of the tooth makes the prosthesis fall off; a fracture of the prosthesis belongs in the comment.
A pontic rarely rests on an implant: it happens when an implant, badly placed, could not be loaded and the bridge was made over it. Check that it is not an implant-supported crown.
A position cannot carry both a bridge pontic and a removable denture tooth.
Core build-up or filling under a crown: visible on radiographs only.
Caries possible under or at the margin of a crown.
Cervical abrasion or erosion lesion possible beyond the crown margin (recession): on a tooth crowned long ago the root may be exposed and worn.
Systematic or frequent coexistence.
Parapulpal pins = amalgam retention.
A crown on a tooth missing AM is only possible on an implant.
An implant abutment implies an implant.
The "space" attribute only applies to a tooth missing AM.
Implant: suggest the abutment, then the superstructure (crown, pontic or attachment).
Tooth missing AM between two present teeth, with nothing replacing it: suggest open / closed space. A pontic, a denture tooth or an implant already occupies the space.
Apicectomy: suggest the root filling.
Contiguous abutment / pontic members: create the bridge group.
Radiographs were obtained from a treating dentist: they are expected among the dental images available (possible inconsistency).
Photographs were obtained from a treating dentist: they are expected among the dental images available (possible inconsistency).
Root post: suggest the root filling (a post is placed in a treated canal).
A date of the record (envelope, header of the form, sections) before 1 January 1900 or after today is probably a typing error; it is reported, never refused.
A wisdom tooth missing during life (agenesis or extraction) is simply recorded as missing AM: an open or closed space describes the gap between two teeth and does not apply to it.
A crown (bridge abutments included), unless it is borne by an implant, generally comes with a root canal treatment: suggest it.
A crown (bridge abutments included), unless it is borne by an implant, is generally retained by parapulpal pins or by a root post: suggest them.

Files annexed for a type of image: their number is expected to be the number of digital images of that type given in field 615 (possible inconsistency, never blocking; the numbers are not deduced from the files).

Names of persons are written as on the forms of identification: a family name in a field of its own in capital letters (DUPRÉ); a name in one field as forename then FAMILY NAME (Jean DUPONT). Data-entry interfaces write a family name in capitals as it is typed and show the convention as an example; the validator reminds it, never blocking: a family name with a lower-case letter, a name in one field with fewer capital letters than min_capitals ("Jean Michel Dupont" is reminded, "Jean DUC" is not).

comparison.definition: Relations used when comparing an AM record with a PM record. They never restrict data entry.

equivalent.rationale: According to experts, the same lesion is coded as caries or as substance loss: equivalent for comparison.

generalisation.rule: A less specific value (parent, 'unspecified', 'unknown') is compatible with any of its more specific values.

explainable_am_to_pm.rule: Changes explainable by treatment or loss between the AM record date and death.

parameters.definition: How the comparison reads an AM finding that is absent in PM, and a PM finding that is absent in AM. Validated by the expert; the comparison remains a sorting tool. numbering_shift_segments: groups of neighbouring positions of a quadrant (4-5: premolars; 6-8: molars) inside which two experts may number the same teeth differently (drift after an old extraction, orthodontic extraction of a premolar): when a tooth missing AM is found present in PM there, the comparison also reads the teeth of the group in their order.

person.definition: Optional checks of the person, chosen by the expert when comparing; none by default. Sex: two different values among sex_decisive set the pair aside; any other value on either side (other, unknown, not entered) leaves the check indeterminate. Age: the AM age (on the day of disappearance) is compared with the classes of age that the PM estimate covers (classes bounded by age_class_limits: 0-12, 12-25, 25-50, 50 and over); an age that comes within the margin of a class is compatible with it, strictly (with a margin of 10 years, 51 and 59 are compatible with 25-50, 60 is not; 41 is compatible with 50 and over). The margin is that of the context of the records: in routine work the time between disappearance and discovery is unknown and may be long.

record.context.label: Context
record.context.definition: Disaster, or routine work on an individual case.

record.context.routine.label: Routine
record.context.routine.definition: An individual case: one missing person, one unidentified body.

record.disaster.label: Disaster
record.disaster.definition: Disaster the record relates to: place, nature and date.

record.disaster.name.label: Name of the disaster
record.disaster.name.definition: Name given to the disaster by those in charge; the same name on every record of the disaster.

record.case.label: Case
record.case.definition: Individual case of routine work: number, place, date of opening.

record.person.label: Person
record.person.definition: Missing person (AM record) or unidentified remains (PM record: sex only).

record.person.age.label: Age on the day of disappearance (years)

dental.provider.attachments.administrati.label: Administrative record
dental.provider.attachments.administrati.definition: Administrative record of the patient (identity, contact details, appointments, invoices...). Not on the Interpol form: printed with the other documents.

record.context.label: Contexte
record.context.definition: Catastrophe, ou travail de routine sur un cas individuel.

record.context.routine.label: Routine
record.context.routine.definition: Un cas individuel : une personne disparue, un corps non identifié.

record.disaster.label: Catastrophe
record.disaster.definition: Catastrophe à laquelle la fiche se rapporte : lieu, nature et date.

record.disaster.name.label: Nom de la catastrophe
record.disaster.name.definition: Nom donné à la catastrophe par ses responsables ; le même nom sur toutes les fiches de la catastrophe.

record.case.label: Dossier
record.case.definition: Dossier individuel du travail de routine : numéro, lieu, date d'ouverture.

record.person.label: Personne
record.person.definition: Personne disparue (fiche AM) ou restes humains non identifiés (fiche PM : sexe uniquement).

record.person.age.label: Âge le jour de la disparition (années)

dental.surface.O.label: Occlusale / incisive
dental.surface.O.definition: Face occlusale (dents postérieures) ou bord incisif (dents antérieures).

dental.status.examined.label: Examinée
dental.status.examined.definition: La position a été examinée ; la présence et les constatations sont renseignées.

dental.status.examined_no_finding.label: Présente saine
dental.status.examined_no_finding.definition: La dent est présente et rien n'est à signaler : ni lésion, ni usure, ni restauration, ni traitement, ni appareil, ni bijou, ni anomalie de position.

dental.status.no_information.label: Sans information
dental.status.no_information.definition: Rien ne peut être dit sur cette position (ex. fragment de mâchoire manquant, aucun document AM couvrant cette dent). Ce n'est pas une constatation négative.

dental.source.photograph.label: Photographie
dental.source.photograph.definition: Photographie. Les photos intra-buccales prises au miroir sont inversées.

dental.presence.present.label: Présente
dental.presence.present.definition: Dent (ou sa couronne) présente et visible en bouche.

dental.presence.partially_erupted.label: Éruption partielle
dental.presence.partially_erupted.definition: Dent en cours d'éruption, partiellement visible.

dental.presence.impacted_partially_visib.label: Enclavée (partiellement visible)
dental.presence.impacted_partially_visib.definition: Dent qui émerge en bouche mais bloquée dans son éruption (surtout dents de sagesse).

dental.presence.unerupted.label: Incluse
dental.presence.unerupted.definition: Dent incluse dont la présence est confirmée (en général radiographiquement).

dental.presence.not_visible.label: Non visible
dental.presence.not_visible.definition: Non visible à l'examen clinique ; présence non confirmable sans imagerie (ex. dent incluse suspectée chez l'enfant).

dental.presence.root_remnant.label: Racine résiduelle
dental.presence.root_remnant.definition: Seule la racine (ou une partie) subsiste. Volontairement peu précis.

dental.presence.missing_am.label: Absente AM
dental.presence.missing_am.definition: Dent perdue du vivant (alvéole cicatrisée ou en cours, ou dent remplacée par prothèse ou implant). Couvre extraction et agénésie : la cause n'est pas renseignée.

dental.presence.missing_pm.label: Absente PM
dental.presence.missing_pm.definition: Dent perdue après le décès (alvéole vide sans cicatrisation).

dental.presence.space.open.label: Espace ouvert
dental.presence.space.open.definition: L'espace laissé par la dent absente persiste.

dental.presence.space.closed.label: Espace fermé
dental.presence.space.closed.definition: L'espace laissé par la dent absente s'est refermé.

dental.aspect.silver_metal.label: Métal argenté
dental.aspect.silver_metal.definition: Métal argenté (amalgame pour une obturation ; couronne métallique ou préformée en acier pour une couronne).

dental.aspect.metal_ceramic.label: Céramo-métallique
dental.aspect.metal_ceramic.definition: Couronne à armature métallique entièrement recouverte de céramique.

dental.aspect.metal_with_facing.label: Métal avec incrustation / facette
dental.aspect.metal_with_facing.definition: Couronne métallique avec une incrustation ou facette couleur dent sur la seule face visible (traitement ancien).

dental.finding.substance_loss.label: Perte de substance
dental.finding.substance_loss.definition: Perte de substance dentaire d'origine non précisée (carieuse ou non).

dental.finding.tooth_fracture.label: Fracture dentaire
dental.finding.tooth_fracture.definition: Fracture de la dent elle-même (pas de la mâchoire, voir le groupe jaw_fracture).

dental.finding.filling.label: Obturation
dental.finding.filling.definition: Restauration intracoronaire directe ou indirecte, sans distinction.

dental.finding.crown.label: Couronne
dental.finding.crown.definition: Couronne prothétique recouvrant toute la couronne clinique, sur dent naturelle ou sur implant.

dental.finding.pontic.label: Intermédiaire de bridge
dental.finding.pontic.definition: Élément intermédiaire de bridge remplaçant une dent absente. Une racine résiduelle peut subsister dessous.

dental.finding.denture_tooth.label: Dent de prothèse amovible
dental.finding.denture_tooth.definition: Dent d'une prothèse amovible. Une racine résiduelle peut subsister dessous.

dental.finding.denture_attachment.label: Attachement de prothèse amovible
dental.finding.denture_attachment.definition: Dispositif de rétention d'une prothèse amovible, sur implant ou sur racine.

dental.finding.periodontal_pathology.label: Pathologie parodontale
dental.finding.periodontal_pathology.definition: Atteinte parodontale de la dent. Volontairement peu précis : simple mention.

dental.finding.orthodontic_appliance.label: Appareil orthodontique
dental.finding.orthodontic_appliance.definition: Appareil orthodontique fixé sur la dent ou la recouvrant.

dental.finding.splint.label: Contention
dental.finding.splint.definition: Contention collée incluant cette dent. Les segments sont décrits par le groupe « splint ».

dental.position.rotation.label: Rotation
dental.position.rotation.definition: Rotation autour du grand axe, nommée d'après la direction prise par la face MÉSIALE. Indépendante de la vue et du quadrant.

dental.position.rotation.MV.label: Mésio-vestibulaire
dental.position.rotation.MV.definition: La face mésiale est tournée vers le vestibule (équivaut à disto-linguale).

dental.position.rotation.ML.label: Mésio-linguale
dental.position.rotation.ML.definition: La face mésiale est tournée vers la langue ou le palais (équivaut à disto-vestibulaire).

dental.position.migration.label: Migration
dental.position.migration.definition: Déplacement de la dent le long de l'arcade.

dental.group.bridge.label: Bridge
dental.group.bridge.definition: Bridge fixe. Membres : dents portant une couronne pilier ou un intermédiaire ; créé automatiquement à partir des membres contigus, l'expert peut le scinder (17-14 ou 17-16 + 15-14).

dental.group.splint.label: Segment de contention
dental.group.splint.definition: Segment continu de contention collée. Une contention rompue donne plusieurs segments (ex. 43-41 et 31-32).

dental.group.diastema.label: Diastème
dental.group.diastema.definition: Espace entre deux dents adjacentes présentes.

dental.group.jaw_fragment_missing.label: Fragment de mâchoire manquant
dental.group.jaw_fragment_missing.definition: Fragment de mâchoire manquant, contenant 0 à n positions dentaires. Voir aussi le formulaire PM, rubrique « État des mâchoires » (fragments).

dental.group.jaw_fracture.label: Fracture de mâchoire
dental.group.jaw_fracture.definition: Trait de fracture de la mâchoire, situé entre deux positions dentaires adjacentes.

dental.arch.removable_denture.label: Prothèse amovible
dental.arch.removable_denture.definition: Prothèse amovible sur une arcade. La prothèse complète est déduite quand toutes les dents de l'arcade portent une dent de prothèse amovible ; les dents de sagesse sont facultatives, car elles ne sont souvent pas montées sur une prothèse complète.

rule.R-D-001.rationale: « Présente saine » : rien d'autre ne peut être renseigné (appareil, contention et bijou incompatibles).

rule.R-D-002.rationale: Une dent présente saine n'a aucun problème associé (ni usure, ni perte de substance, ni fracture, ni version, ni rotation…) : extension aux anomalies de position, par cohérence avec la règle précédente.

rule.R-D-003.rationale: Sans information : aucune donnée sur la position.

rule.R-D-004.rationale: Une position examinée doit avoir une présence.

rule.R-D-005.rationale: Les dents d'un fragment de mâchoire manquant reçoivent par défaut le statut « sans information » (modifiable).

rule.R-D-006.rationale: Couronne : défaut de l'émail recouvert par la couronne.

rule.R-D-009.rationale: Couronne : l'attrition concerne une face recouverte par la couronne.

rule.R-D-010.rationale: Couronne : une fracture coronaire de la dent fait tomber la prothèse ; une fracture de la prothèse relève du commentaire.

rule.R-D-011.rationale: Un intermédiaire repose rarement sur un implant : cela arrive quand l'implant, mal placé, n'a pas pu être mis en charge et que le bridge a été fait par-dessus. Vérifier qu'il ne s'agit pas d'une couronne sur implant.

rule.R-D-012.rationale: Une position ne peut porter à la fois un intermédiaire de bridge et une dent de prothèse amovible.

rule.R-D-013.rationale: Reconstitution ou obturation sous couronne : visible en radiographie seulement.

rule.R-D-014.rationale: Carie possible sous ou en limite de couronne.

rule.R-D-015.rationale: Lésion cervicale d'abrasion ou d'érosion possible au-delà du bord de la couronne (récession) : sur une dent couronnée depuis longtemps, la racine peut être apparente et abrasée par l'usure.

rule.R-D-018.rationale: Une couronne sur une dent absente AM n'est possible que sur implant.

rule.R-D-019.rationale: Un pilier implantaire suppose un implant.

rule.R-D-020.rationale: L'attribut « espace » ne s'applique qu'à une dent absente AM.

rule.R-D-021.rationale: Implant : proposer pilier puis supra-structure (couronne, intermédiaire ou attachement).

rule.R-D-022.rationale: Dent absente AM entre deux dents présentes, sans élément de remplacement : proposer espace ouvert / fermé. Un intermédiaire de bridge, une dent de prothèse amovible ou un implant occupent déjà l'espace.

rule.R-D-023.rationale: Résection apicale : proposer le traitement endodontique.

rule.R-D-024.rationale: Membres contigus pilier / intermédiaire : créer le groupe bridge.

mapping.plassdata_v7.mtl.label: Perte de substance - Carie (lésion carieuse)
mapping.plassdata_v7.mtl.note: EN « Marked tooth loss » / FR « Lésion carieuse (ou perte de volume) » : importé comme perte de substance (valeur la moins précise).

mapping.plassdata_v7.tcc.note: Le libellé français de PlassData décrit une couronne métallique à incrustation ou facette céramique (aspect « métal avec incrustation / facette »), un soin ancien mais encore rencontré ; le libellé anglais dit « couronne couleur dent ». La lecture française est retenue.

mapping.plassdata_v7.fud.note: Niveau arcade. Chaque dent sur laquelle le code est saisi reçoit aussi une dent prothétique (absente ante mortem par défaut) ; saisi sur des dents mandibulaires, la prothèse complète est enregistrée à l'arcade inférieure.

mapping.plassdata_v7.vis.note: État parent redondant : remplacé par la valeur précise.

mapping.plassdata_v7.cro.note: Import : la dent est ajoutée au groupe d'encombrement de son secteur.

mapping.plassdata_v7.dia.note: Un diastème se renseigne sur les deux dents voisines concernées (ex. dia sur 31 et sur 41, ou dia sur « 31-41 » en saisie multiple) : le groupe est formé de ces deux dents.

mapping.plassdata_v7.spa.note: Code historique : importé en commentaire libre (arcade).

mapping.plassdata_v7.dis.note: Code historique : importé en commentaire libre (arcade).

mapping.plassdata_v7.clr.note: Convention Perdrix, telle que vue sur l'odontogramme (vue éclatée, vestibulaire du côté externe de chaque arcade) : le sens horaire tourne la face mésiale vers le lingual (ML) dans les quadrants 1 et 3, vers le vestibule (MV) dans les quadrants 2 et 4. Sur le formulaire Interpol, le code est écrit dans la case de la dent et MV ou ML est précisé en page de renseignements complémentaires (champ 700). Des données saisies avec un autre outil peuvent suivre une autre lecture : à vérifier à l'import.

mapping.plassdata_v7.ccr.note: Convention Perdrix, telle que vue sur l'odontogramme (vue éclatée, vestibulaire du côté externe de chaque arcade) : le sens anti-horaire tourne la face mésiale vers le vestibule (MV) dans les quadrants 1 et 3, vers le lingual (ML) dans les quadrants 2 et 4. Sur le formulaire Interpol, le code est écrit dans la case de la dent et MV ou ML est précisé en page de renseignements complémentaires (champ 700). Des données saisies avec un autre outil peuvent suivre une autre lecture : à vérifier à l'import.

mapping.plassdata_v7.mre.note: Remplacement non précisé : jamais proposé à la saisie.

comparison.equivalent.caries_substance_l.rationale: Selon les experts, la même lésion est codée carie ou perte de substance : équivalentes pour la comparaison.

dental.provider.records_from.label: Début de la prise en charge

dental.provider.records_to.label: Fin de la prise en charge

dental.provider.attachments.administrati.label: Dossier administratif
dental.provider.attachments.administrati.definition: Dossier administratif du patient (identité, coordonnées, rendez-vous, factures…). Absent du formulaire Interpol : imprimé avec les autres pièces.

dental.dentition.primary.label: Dentition temporaire
dental.dentition.primary.definition: Seules des dents temporaires sont présentes en bouche.

dental.dentition.mixed.label: Dentition mixte
dental.dentition.mixed.definition: Des dents temporaires et des dents permanentes sont présentes en bouche.

dental.dentition.permanent.label: Dentition permanente
dental.dentition.permanent.definition: Seules des dents permanentes sont présentes en bouche.

rule.R-D-025.rationale: Des radiographies ont été obtenues d'un dentiste traitant : elles sont attendues dans les images dentaires disponibles (incohérence possible).

rule.R-D-026.rationale: Des photographies ont été obtenues d'un dentiste traitant : elles sont attendues dans les images dentaires disponibles (incohérence possible).

dental.finding.root_post.label: Tenon radiculaire
dental.finding.root_post.definition: Tenon placé dans un canal radiculaire pour retenir une restauration (tenon vissé, inlay-core).

rule.R-D-027.rationale: Tenon radiculaire : proposer le traitement endodontique (un tenon est placé dans un canal traité).

dental.source.intraoral_scan.label: Scanner intra-oral
dental.source.intraoral_scan.definition: Empreinte optique intra-buccale (modèle tridimensionnel de la surface des dents).

rule.R-D-028.rationale: Une date de la fiche (enveloppe, en-tête du formulaire, rubriques) antérieure au 1er janvier 1900 ou postérieure à aujourd'hui est probablement une erreur de saisie ; elle est signalée, jamais refusée.

rule.R-D-029.rationale: Une dent de sagesse absente du vivant (agénésie ou extraction) s'enregistre simplement « absente ante mortem » : l'espace ouvert ou fermé décrit l'écart entre deux dents et ne s'y applique pas.

rule.R-D-030.rationale: Une couronne (piliers de bridge compris), sauf sur implant, va en général avec un traitement endodontique : le proposer.

rule.R-D-031.rationale: Une couronne (piliers de bridge compris), sauf sur implant, est en général retenue par des tenons dentinaires ou un tenon radiculaire : les proposer.

rule.R-D-032.rationale: Pièces jointes d'un type d'image : leur nombre devrait être le nombre d'images numériques de ce type indiqué au champ 615 (incohérence possible, jamais bloquante ; les nombres ne sont pas déduits des pièces).

rule.R-D-033.rationale: Les noms de personnes s'écrivent comme sur les formulaires d'identification : un nom de famille dans son propre champ, en capitales (DUPRÉ) ; un nom en un seul champ, prénom puis NOM de famille (Jean DUPONT). Les interfaces de saisie mettent en capitales le nom de famille à la frappe et montrent la convention en exemple ; le validateur la rappelle, sans jamais bloquer : un nom de famille qui contient une minuscule, un nom en un seul champ qui compte moins de lettres capitales que min_capitals (« Jean Michel Dupont » est signalé, « Jean DUC » ne l'est pas).

record.context.label: Contexto
record.context.definition: Catástrofe, o trabajo rutinario sobre un caso individual.

record.context.routine.label: Rutina
record.context.routine.definition: Un caso individual: una persona desaparecida, un cadáver sin identificar.

record.disaster.label: Catástrofe
record.disaster.definition: Catástrofe a la que se refiere la ficha: lugar, tipo y fecha.

record.disaster.name.label: Nombre de la catástrofe
record.disaster.name.definition: Nombre dado a la catástrofe por sus responsables; el mismo nombre en todas las fichas de la catástrofe.

record.case.label: Expediente
record.case.definition: Expediente individual del trabajo rutinario: número, lugar, fecha de apertura.

record.person.label: Persona
record.person.definition: Persona desaparecida (ficha AM) o restos humanos sin identificar (ficha PM: solo el sexo).

record.person.age.label: Edad el día de la desaparición (años)

dental.surface.O.label: Oclusal / incisal
dental.surface.O.definition: Cara oclusal (dientes posteriores) o borde incisal (dientes anteriores).

dental.status.examined.label: Examinado
dental.status.examined.definition: La posición se ha examinado; se indican la presencia y los hallazgos.

dental.status.examined_no_finding.label: Presente sano
dental.status.examined_no_finding.definition: El diente está presente y no hay nada que señalar: ni lesión, ni desgaste, ni restauración, ni tratamiento, ni aparato, ni joya, ni anomalía de posición.

dental.status.no_information.label: Sin información
dental.status.no_information.definition: No se puede decir nada de esta posición (p. ej., fragmento de maxilar ausente, ningún documento AM que cubra este diente). No es un hallazgo negativo.

dental.source.dental_record.label: Historia clínica dental
dental.source.dental_record.definition: Historia clínica dental escrita (odontograma, notas, facturas).

dental.source.photograph.label: Fotografía
dental.source.photograph.definition: Fotografía. Las fotografías intraorales tomadas con espejo están invertidas.

dental.presence.present.label: Presente
dental.presence.present.definition: Diente (o su corona) presente y visible en boca.

dental.presence.impacted_partially_visib.label: Enclavado (parcialmente visible)
dental.presence.impacted_partially_visib.definition: Diente que asoma en boca pero cuya erupción está bloqueada (sobre todo cordales).

dental.presence.unerupted.label: Incluido
dental.presence.unerupted.definition: Diente incluido cuya presencia está confirmada (en general por radiografía).

dental.presence.not_visible.label: No visible
dental.presence.not_visible.definition: No visible en el examen clínico; presencia no confirmable sin imagen (p. ej., diente incluido sospechado en un niño).

dental.presence.root_remnant.label: Resto radicular
dental.presence.root_remnant.definition: Solo queda la raíz (o una parte). Deliberadamente poco preciso.

dental.presence.missing_am.label: Ausente AM
dental.presence.missing_am.definition: Diente perdido en vida (alvéolo cicatrizado o en cicatrización, o diente sustituido por una prótesis o un implante). Incluye la extracción y la agenesia: la causa no se indica.

dental.presence.missing_pm.label: Ausente PM
dental.presence.missing_pm.definition: Diente perdido después de la muerte (alvéolo vacío sin cicatrización).

dental.presence.space.open.label: Espacio abierto
dental.presence.space.open.definition: El espacio dejado por el diente ausente persiste.

dental.presence.space.closed.label: Espacio cerrado
dental.presence.space.closed.definition: El espacio dejado por el diente ausente se ha cerrado.

dental.aspect.silver_metal.label: Metal plateado
dental.aspect.silver_metal.definition: Metal plateado (amalgama en una obturación; corona metálica o preformada de acero en una corona).

dental.aspect.tooth_coloured.label: Color diente
dental.aspect.tooth_coloured.definition: Color diente (composite, cerámica, ionómero de vidrio…).

dental.aspect.metal_ceramic.label: Metal-cerámica
dental.aspect.metal_ceramic.definition: Corona con estructura metálica totalmente recubierta de cerámica.

dental.aspect.metal_with_facing.label: Metal con frente estético
dental.aspect.metal_with_facing.definition: Corona metálica con un frente o carilla color diente solo en la cara visible (tratamiento antiguo).

dental.finding.substance_loss.label: Pérdida de sustancia
dental.finding.substance_loss.definition: Pérdida de sustancia dental de origen no precisado (cariosa o no).

dental.finding.tooth_fracture.label: Fractura dental
dental.finding.tooth_fracture.definition: Fractura del propio diente (no del maxilar: véase el grupo jaw_fracture).

dental.finding.filling.label: Obturación
dental.finding.filling.definition: Restauración intracoronaria directa o indirecta, sin distinción.

dental.finding.crown.label: Corona
dental.finding.crown.definition: Corona protésica que cubre toda la corona clínica, sobre diente natural o sobre implante.

dental.finding.pontic.label: Póntico
dental.finding.pontic.definition: Elemento intermedio de un puente que sustituye a un diente ausente. Puede quedar un resto radicular debajo.

dental.finding.denture_tooth.label: Diente de prótesis removible
dental.finding.denture_tooth.definition: Diente de una prótesis removible. Puede quedar un resto radicular debajo.

dental.finding.denture_attachment.label: Atache de prótesis removible
dental.finding.denture_attachment.definition: Dispositivo de retención de una prótesis removible, sobre implante o sobre raíz.

dental.finding.periodontal_pathology.label: Patología periodontal
dental.finding.periodontal_pathology.definition: Afectación periodontal del diente. Deliberadamente poco preciso: simple mención.

dental.finding.orthodontic_appliance.label: Aparato de ortodoncia
dental.finding.orthodontic_appliance.definition: Aparato de ortodoncia fijado al diente o que lo cubre.

dental.finding.splint.label: Férula
dental.finding.splint.definition: Férula adherida que incluye este diente. Los segmentos se describen con el grupo «splint».

dental.position.infraposition.label: Infraposición / infraoclusión
dental.position.infraposition.definition: Diente por debajo del plano oclusal.

dental.position.supraposition.label: Supraposición (extrusión)
dental.position.supraposition.definition: Diente por encima del plano oclusal (extrusión).

dental.position.rotation.label: Rotación
dental.position.rotation.definition: Rotación alrededor del eje mayor, nombrada según la dirección que toma la cara MESIAL. Independiente de la vista y del cuadrante.

dental.position.rotation.MV.label: Mesiovestibular
dental.position.rotation.MV.definition: La cara mesial está girada hacia el vestíbulo (equivale a distolingual).

dental.position.rotation.ML.label: Mesiolingual
dental.position.rotation.ML.definition: La cara mesial está girada hacia la lengua o el paladar (equivale a distovestibular).

dental.position.migration.label: Migración
dental.position.migration.definition: Desplazamiento del diente a lo largo de la arcada.

dental.group.bridge.label: Puente
dental.group.bridge.definition: Puente fijo. Miembros: dientes que llevan una corona pilar o un póntico; se crea automáticamente a partir de los miembros contiguos, y el experto puede dividirlo (17-14 o 17-16 + 15-14).

dental.group.splint.label: Segmento de férula
dental.group.splint.definition: Segmento continuo de férula adherida. Una férula rota da varios segmentos (p. ej., 43-41 y 31-32).

dental.group.crowding.label: Apiñamiento
dental.group.crowding.definition: Apiñamiento de un sector de la arcada.

dental.group.diastema.label: Diastema
dental.group.diastema.definition: Espacio entre dos dientes adyacentes presentes.

dental.group.jaw_fragment_missing.label: Fragmento de maxilar ausente
dental.group.jaw_fragment_missing.definition: Fragmento de maxilar ausente, que contiene de 0 a n posiciones dentales. Véase también el formulario PM, apartado «Estado de la mandíbula» (fragmentos).

dental.group.jaw_fracture.label: Fractura de maxilar
dental.group.jaw_fracture.definition: Trazo de fractura del maxilar, situado entre dos posiciones dentales adyacentes.

dental.arch.removable_denture.label: Prótesis removible
dental.arch.removable_denture.definition: Prótesis removible sobre una arcada. La prótesis completa se deduce cuando todos los dientes de la arcada llevan un diente de prótesis removible; los cordales son facultativos, porque a menudo no se montan en una prótesis completa.

rule.R-D-001.rationale: «Presente sano»: no se puede indicar nada más (aparato, férula y joya incompatibles).

rule.R-D-002.rationale: Un diente presente sano no tiene ningún problema asociado (ni desgaste, ni pérdida de sustancia, ni fractura, ni versión, ni rotación…): extensión a las anomalías de posición, por coherencia con la regla anterior.

rule.R-D-003.rationale: Sin información: ningún dato sobre la posición.

rule.R-D-004.rationale: Una posición examinada debe tener una presencia.

rule.R-D-005.rationale: Los dientes de un fragmento de maxilar ausente reciben por defecto el estado «sin información» (modificable).

rule.R-D-006.rationale: Corona: defecto del esmalte cubierto por la corona.

rule.R-D-009.rationale: Corona: la atrición afecta a una cara cubierta por la corona.

rule.R-D-010.rationale: Corona: una fractura coronaria del diente hace caer la prótesis; una fractura de la prótesis corresponde al comentario.

rule.R-D-011.rationale: Un póntico rara vez se apoya en un implante: ocurre cuando el implante, mal colocado, no pudo cargarse y el puente se hizo por encima. Compruebe que no se trata de una corona sobre implante.

rule.R-D-012.rationale: Una posición no puede llevar a la vez un póntico y un diente de prótesis removible.

rule.R-D-013.rationale: Reconstrucción u obturación bajo corona: visible solo en radiografía.

rule.R-D-014.rationale: Caries posible bajo la corona o en su margen.

rule.R-D-015.rationale: Lesión cervical de abrasión o de erosión posible más allá del margen de la corona (recesión): en un diente coronado desde hace tiempo, la raíz puede quedar expuesta y desgastada.

rule.R-D-018.rationale: Una corona sobre un diente ausente AM solo es posible sobre implante.

rule.R-D-019.rationale: Un pilar de implante supone un implante.

rule.R-D-020.rationale: El atributo «espacio» solo se aplica a un diente ausente AM.

rule.R-D-021.rationale: Implante: proponer pilar y después supraestructura (corona, póntico o atache).

rule.R-D-022.rationale: Diente ausente AM entre dos dientes presentes, sin elemento de sustitución: proponer espacio abierto / cerrado. Un póntico, un diente de prótesis removible o un implante ya ocupan el espacio.

rule.R-D-024.rationale: Miembros contiguos pilar / póntico: crear el grupo puente.

mapping.plassdata_v7.mtl.label: Pérdida de sustancia - Caries (lesión de caries)
mapping.plassdata_v7.mtl.note: EN «Marked tooth loss» / FR «Lésion carieuse (ou perte de volume)»: se importa como pérdida de sustancia (el valor menos preciso).

mapping.plassdata_v7.tcc.note: La etiqueta francesa de PlassData describe una corona metálica con incrustación o frente cerámico (aspecto «metal con frente estético»), un tratamiento antiguo pero aún presente; la etiqueta inglesa dice «corona color diente». Se adopta la lectura francesa.

mapping.plassdata_v7.fud.note: Nivel de arcada. Cada diente en el que se introduce el código recibe también un diente protésico (ausente ante mortem por defecto); introducido en dientes mandibulares, la prótesis completa se registra en la arcada inferior.

mapping.plassdata_v7.vis.note: Estado padre redundante: sustituido por el valor preciso.

mapping.plassdata_v7.cro.note: Importación: el diente se añade al grupo de apiñamiento de su sector.

mapping.plassdata_v7.dia.note: Un diastema se indica en los dos dientes vecinos afectados (p. ej., dia en 31 y en 41, o dia en «31-41» en la entrada múltiple): el grupo lo forman esos dos dientes.

mapping.plassdata_v7.spa.note: Código histórico: se importa como comentario libre (arcada).

mapping.plassdata_v7.dis.note: Código histórico: se importa como comentario libre (arcada).

mapping.plassdata_v7.clr.note: Convención Perdrix, tal como se ve en el odontograma (vista desplegada, cara vestibular hacia el lado externo de cada arcada): el sentido horario gira la cara mesial hacia lingual (ML) en los cuadrantes 1 y 3, hacia vestibular (MV) en los cuadrantes 2 y 4. En el formulario de Interpol, el código se escribe en la casilla del diente y MV o ML se precisa en la página de información adicional (campo 700). Los datos introducidos con otra herramienta pueden seguir otra lectura: compruébelo al importar.

mapping.plassdata_v7.ccr.note: Convención Perdrix, tal como se ve en el odontograma (vista desplegada, cara vestibular hacia el lado externo de cada arcada): el sentido antihorario gira la cara mesial hacia vestibular (MV) en los cuadrantes 1 y 3, hacia lingual (ML) en los cuadrantes 2 y 4. En el formulario de Interpol, el código se escribe en la casilla del diente y MV o ML se precisa en la página de información adicional (campo 700). Los datos introducidos con otra herramienta pueden seguir otra lectura: compruébelo al importar.

mapping.plassdata_v7.mre.note: Sustitución no precisada: nunca se propone en la entrada.

comparison.equivalent.caries_substance_l.rationale: Según los expertos, la misma lesión se codifica como caries o como pérdida de sustancia: equivalentes para la comparación.

dental.provider.attachments.administrati.label: Historia administrativa
dental.provider.attachments.administrati.definition: Historia administrativa del paciente (identidad, datos de contacto, citas, facturas…). No figura en el formulario de Interpol: se imprime con los demás documentos.

dental.dentition.primary.label: Dentición primaria
dental.dentition.primary.definition: Solo hay dientes temporales en boca.

dental.dentition.mixed.label: Dentición mixta
dental.dentition.mixed.definition: Hay dientes temporales y dientes permanentes en boca.

dental.dentition.permanent.label: Dentición permanente
dental.dentition.permanent.definition: Solo hay dientes permanentes en boca.

rule.R-D-025.rationale: Se obtuvieron radiografías de un odontólogo: se esperan en las imágenes dentales disponibles (posible incoherencia).

rule.R-D-026.rationale: Se obtuvieron fotografías de un odontólogo: se esperan en las imágenes dentales disponibles (posible incoherencia).

dental.finding.root_post.label: Perno radicular
dental.finding.root_post.definition: Perno colocado en un conducto radicular para retener una restauración (perno roscado, muñón colado).

rule.R-D-027.rationale: Perno radicular: proponer el tratamiento endodóntico (un perno se coloca en un conducto tratado).

dental.source.intraoral_scan.label: Escáner intraoral
dental.source.intraoral_scan.definition: Impresión óptica intraoral (modelo tridimensional de la superficie de los dientes).

rule.R-D-028.rationale: Una fecha de la ficha (envoltorio, encabezado del formulario, apartados) anterior al 1 de enero de 1900 o posterior a hoy es probablemente un error de escritura; se señala, nunca se rechaza.

rule.R-D-029.rationale: Un cordal ausente en vida (agenesia o extracción) se registra simplemente como «ausente ante mortem»: el espacio abierto o cerrado describe la separación entre dos dientes y no se aplica.

rule.R-D-030.rationale: Una corona (pilares de puente incluidos), salvo sobre implante, suele ir con un tratamiento endodóntico: proponerlo.

rule.R-D-031.rationale: Una corona (pilares de puente incluidos), salvo sobre implante, suele retenerse con pines dentinarios o un perno radicular: proponerlos.

rule.R-D-032.rationale: Archivos adjuntos de un tipo de imagen: su número debería ser el número de imágenes digitales de ese tipo indicado en el campo 615 (posible incoherencia, nunca bloqueante; los números no se deducen de los archivos).

rule.R-D-033.rationale: Los nombres de personas se escriben como en los formularios de identificación: unos apellidos en su propio campo, en mayúsculas (DUPRÉ); un nombre en un solo campo, nombre y después APELLIDOS (Jean DUPONT). Las interfaces de entrada ponen los apellidos en mayúsculas al teclearlos y muestran la convención como ejemplo; el validador la recuerda, sin bloquear nunca: unos apellidos con una minúscula, un nombre en un solo campo con menos letras mayúsculas que min_capitals («Jean Michel Dupont» se señala, «Jean DUC» no).

mtl.note: EN "Marked tooth loss" / FR "Lésion carieuse (ou perte de volume)": imported as substance loss (least specific value).

tcc.note: The French PlassData label describes a metal crown with a ceramic facing or inlay (aspect metal_with_facing), an older treatment still met in practice; the English label reads "tooth coloured crown". The French reading is the one retained.

fud.note: Arch level. Each tooth the code is entered on also receives a denture tooth (missing ante mortem by default); entered on mandibular teeth, the complete denture is recorded on the lower arch.

fis.note: Surface O by default, can be changed.

vis.note: Redundant parent state: replaced by the specific value.

cro.note: Import: the tooth is added to the crowding group of its sector.

dia.note: A diastema is recorded on both neighbouring teeth it lies between (e.g. dia on 31 and on 41, or dia on "31-41" in multiple entry): the group is made of those two teeth.

spa.note: Historical code: imported as a free-text comment (arch).

dis.note: Historical code: imported as a free-text comment (arch).

clr.note: Perdrix convention, as seen on the odontogram (exploded view, vestibular on the outer side of each arch): clockwise turns the mesial surface lingually (ML) in quadrants 1 and 3, vestibularly (MV) in quadrants 2 and 4. On the Interpol form the code is written in the tooth box and MV or ML is specified on the additional information page (field 700). Data entered with another tool may follow another reading: to be checked at import.

ccr.note: Perdrix convention, as seen on the odontogram (exploded view, vestibular on the outer side of each arch): counterclockwise turns the mesial surface vestibularly (MV) in quadrants 1 and 3, lingually (ML) in quadrants 2 and 4. On the Interpol form the code is written in the tooth box and MV or ML is specified on the additional information page (field 700). Data entered with another tool may follow another reading: to be checked at import.

mre.note: Unspecified replacement: never offered for data entry.

tooth_text_field.serialisation: Text of the field of a form box (630_{FDI}, FDI of the permanent tooth), item by item, separated by ", ": each item in words (labels of the norm in the language of the form), then its code in parentheses, after its details when it has some: "Usure O (attrition - att O)", "Présente saine (vis-pre-nad)", "Obturation MO (couleur dent - uif-tcf MO)". When this does not hold in max_chars characters, the box carries the codes only, separated by ", ", and the words go to the page 700, under field 630, one line per tooth, with the tooth comment. Items: the presence (its code only when the tooth carries nothing else, vis-pre, or when it is not simply present); then one per finding, with the most specific active code whose target matches it (surfaces after the code, in the order M O D V L); then one per position anomaly; then the groups the tooth belongs to that have a code (crowding, diastema, jaw fracture, missing jaw fragment). A finding without a code of its own takes the code of an equivalent finding (comparison.equivalent), else it is given in words only. A primary tooth is written "<FDI>: " first.

interpol_2023.definition: Fields of the Interpol DVI forms, version 2023 (AM yellow, PM pink), as found in the expert's own copy of the form: technical names of the AcroForm fields, kept for interoperability only (identical in every language of the forms). Only the dental pages are filled: the pages holding the fields 600 to 705. Each entry says where the value of a field comes from in the record.
interpol_2023.syntax: PATH: dot-separated keys from the record (record.*, dental.*), with [n] for an item of a list and [key=value] for the item of a list that has that value. Text field: PATH (dates as DD/MM/YYYY, lists joined by ", "); PATH#i: character i of the date as DDMMYYYY (one character per box); PATH|nonzero: the number, left empty when it is 0; A + B: texts joined by "; "; label:PATH=v: the label of value v when the field holds it. Check box: PATH=v1|v2 (the field is, or contains, one of the values; true for a boolean); PATH>0; PATH? (the field holds something); A or B. Special: 700 = the text of the page 700 (field 700_1); 700=NNN = the page 700 holds an entry for field NNN (column c); true = always checked.

source.definition: Where the blank forms are published: the DVI page of the Interpol website, and the PDF file of each form by language (latest version; checked on 2026-11-13). An application may offer these links to the expert; a web page cannot fetch the files itself (the Interpol website does not allow it: no CORS header), and the files stay under the terms of use of Interpol.

notes: Rue / No: the norm holds the street and its number in one field (street), written in the street box; the number box stays empty.
State / Country: one field in the norm (state_country), written in the State box.
Field 630 has no column a, b or c on the form.
PM field 610: the norm holds one text for the samples taken, written on the page 700 (the form has one box per row).
Signature boxes are left empty: the electronic signatures of the record are described by record_format.signature.

layouts.definition: Rendering conventions, deliberately outside the vocabulary: changing a colour or a pictogram is a patch version and never changes the meaning of a record.

odontogram.definition: Schematic odontogram: exploded view of the two arches, patient's right on the viewer's left, five faces per tooth. Colours and pictograms follow conventions familiar to DVI experts; the pictograms are plain geometric shapes drawn for Perdrix, placed between the tooth and the occlusal plane, never over the tooth.

faces.definition: Surface drawn on each side of the tooth square, by FDI quadrant of the form box.

shapes.definition: Pictograms drawn in a 16 x 16 box with strokes: line [x1, y1, x2, y2], circle [cx, cy, r], rect [x, y, width, height], path (SVG path data), text at [x, y]. "oriented" shapes point away from the occlusal plane (roots).
